validity.recommendation: Leave Diameter blank as recorded -- this is a compression/valve-only expansion with no new mainline pipe, so a blank Diameter (and LengthKnownKm=0, already correct on the sheet) is the accurate value, not a gap. No action needed.
validity.researcher_notes: FERC's environmental assessment for the Gateway Expansion Project (Docket CP18-18, https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-04/CP18-18-EA_0.pdf, downloaded and read in full with pdftotext -layout since the substring screen cannot see inside a 1.7MB PDF) itemizes the entire facility list: an additional 33,000-hp electric compressor unit at Compressor Station 303 (Essex Co NJ), installation of a 36-inch-diameter Main Line BLOCK VALVE (not new pipe) at the Roseland M&R, an electric transformer at the Roseland substation, and replacement of existing 12-inch headers with two new 6-inch ultrasonic meter skids at the Paterson M&R -- no new pipeline segment anywhere. The EA's own System Alternatives section (Sec 3.2) explicitly considered and REJECTED a pipe-looping alternative: 'a 42-inch-diameter pipeline loop extending 5.8 miles would be required... This alternative is not environmentally preferable' -- i.e. Transco built the compression option instead of the loop, so the 42-inch figure in the wiki's combined project list belongs to that rejected alternative, not to what was actually built. Second, independent source: Natural Gas Intelligence's contemporaneous news coverage of FERC's environmental review confirms the same compressor-station/M&R-only scope (https://www.naturalgasintel.com/news/ferc-launches-environmental-review-of-transcos-gateway-expansion-project/). Per the standing compression-only rule (LengthKnownKm=0, Diameter=blank), the sheet's blank Diameter is the correct, confirmed value.
